title: Chief Shepherd of Thy Chosen Sheep
description: Chief Shepherd of Thy Chosen Sheep in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 50, “Prayer for ministers”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Chief Shep-herd of thy cho-sen sheep, From death and sin set free; May ev-ery un-der shep-herd keep His eye, in-tent on thee!

lines: Chief Shepherd of thy chosen sheep,
From death and sin set free;
May every under-shepherd keep
His eye, intent on thee!
With plenteous grace their hearts prepare,
To execute thy will
Compassion, patience, love and care,
And faithfulness and skill.
Inflame their minds with holy zeal
Their flocks to feed and teach;
And let them live, and let them feel
The sacred truths they preach.
Oh, never let the sheep complain
That toys, which fools amuse;
Ambition, pleasure, praise or gain,
Debase the shepherd's views.
He, that for these, forbears to feed
The souls whom Jesus loves;
Whate'er he may profess, or plead,
An idol-shepherd proves.
The sword of God shall break his arm,
A blast shall blind his eye
His word shall have no pow'r to warm,
His gifts shall all grow dry.
O Lord, avert this heavy woe,
Let all thy shepherds say!
And grace, and strength, on each bestow,
To labor while 'tis day.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
